summary: The package ban closes the sibling hunt for the four I/O packages, and I could not escape java.nio.file / java.nio.channels / java.net / javax.net. The CLOCK family is still class-name enumeration and it is still open: System::currentTimeMillis, System::nanoTime and new GregorianCalendar() each reach the real clock from ingest/src/main, compile, and pass the gate -- and the first contradicts _shape's own docstring and the case name that both assert the method-reference form is refused. The false-positive direction has three measured refusals of correct code, one of them the JDK's prescribed idiom for consuming the Clock seam.

findings.title: Four java.lang / classpath routes to the real filesystem pass, one of them the direct sibling of the `.openStream(` entry restored this round
findings.failure_scenario:
MEASURED at the staged bytes: four files under ingest/src/main/java/binjava/ingest/, all compiled clean by javac, all staged, all inside a single `ok 107 business-logic file(s)` line.

(a) `new ProcessBuilder("cat", "/etc/hostname").start()` and `Runtime.getRuntime().exec(new String[]{"curl","-s",url})` -- RUN, printed `P4 hostname=DESKTOP-IDHVM6D`, i.e. the real /etc/hostname, and the second reaches the network. Both are java.lang; no banned package is named.
(b) `P3.class.getResourceAsStream("/binjava/ingest/config.bin")` -- reads a file off the classpath.
(c) `new java.util.zip.ZipFile(name)` -- opens a real path on disk.
(d) `new java.util.logging.FileHandler(path, true)` -- creates and writes a real file.

(b) IS THE ONE THAT BELONGS IN THIS ROUND'S DIFF. `.openStream(` and `.openConnection(` were restored this round with the comment "a URL CAN ARRIVE WITHOUT ITS PACKAGE BEING NAMED -- `var u = getClass().getResource(\"/x\")` imports nothing". `getClass().getResourceAsStream("/x")` is the same call with the two steps fused, names no package either, and is the form people actually write. Restoring two entries against that argument while leaving the fused form out is the same gap the restoration was for.

MINOR rather than major because the scanner header, AGENTS.md and code-structure.md all state plainly that this is a deny-list over source text that cannot be complete, and (a), (c), (d) are honestly inside that disclosure. (b) is not -- it is a listed entry's alias.

findings.title: `LocalDate.now(clock)` -- the JDK's prescribed way to CONSUME an injected Clock -- is refused as "reaches the real clock directly"
`java.net.URI`, `java.net.URLEncoder` and `java.io.FileNotFoundException` are refused although they reach nothing -- the same value-type argument that earned java.time its exemption
findings.failure_scenario:
MEASURED at the staged bytes, ingest/src/main/java/binjava/ingest/F1.java, compiled clean:

    import java.io.FileNotFoundException; import java.net.URI; import java.net.URLEncoder;
    URI u = URI.create("s3://" + bucket + "/" + URLEncoder.encode(name, StandardCharsets.UTF_8));

Three FAIL lines, exit 1: `java.io.File reaches the filesystem directly` (the FileNotFoundException import), `java.net reaches a socket directly` twice.

`URI` and `URLEncoder` open nothing -- URI is a parsed value, URLEncoder is a pure function, and both are the natural types for building an object-store key or endpoint, which is this project's central noun. That is precisely the argument the commit uses to keep java.time off the package list: "`Clock`, `Instant` and `Duration` are value types this project passes across seams". java.net carries value types too, and the split is not stated anywhere.

AND THE STATED COST IS UNDERSTATED. _package's docstring names exactly one cost -- "a hypothetical `java.network` would also match; no such JDK package exists". The real costs are URI/URLEncoder/URLDecoder under `java.net` and every `java.io.File*Exception` under the `java.io.File` prefix, all reachable today, none hypothetical.

MINOR: nothing in the tree trips it (verified -- no non-exempt src/main file names any banned package, so the cell's "MEASURED FREE ON THIS TREE" holds), and a future need is an argument to have. Refusing a refusal is fine; claiming the only cost is a package that does not exist is not.

I could not get past the four I/O package bans: every route I tried into java.nio.file, java.nio.channels, java.net or javax.net names the package in an import or a qualified use, and is refused. The package-over-class-name change does what it claims for those four families.
